findings.reason: The diff turns line 978 into an unconditional `hasAllShortFlags(arg)` check. hasAllShortFlags (945-967) checks each letter on its own, so '-ab' counts as known and isUnknownOptionAsArg returns false at line 226. The branch at line 262 (`!configuration['short-option-groups'] && arg.match(/^-[^-]+/)`) then reads the whole 'ab' as the key at line 264 and sets it.
findings.claim: With short-option-groups off and unknown-options-as-args on, an unknown option like '-ab' made of known single-letter flags is no longer treated as unknown. It gets parsed as a new key 'ab' instead of being passed through to argv._.
findings.evidence: Line 978 now reads `if (hasAllShortFlags(arg)) { return false }`. `hasAllShortFlags` (lines 945-967) checks each letter separately with `hasAnyFlag(letters[j])`, so `-ab` returns true when `a` and `b` are defined, and `isUnknownOption` returns false. In the main loop, the branch at line 262 (`!configuration['short-option-groups'] && arg.match(/^-[^-]+/)`) then reads the whole `ab` as the key (`m = arg.match(/^--?(.+)/)`) and calls setArg on it. Before the change, the guard skipped the per-letter check when grouping was off, so `hasFlagsMatching(arg, ..., normalFlag)` looked up the key `ab`, found nothing, and the arg went through `pushPositional`.
